cases.description: A scheduled Update checks the feeds Core named: a changed source is a success and is downloaded.
A retry checks the feeds Core named; an unchanged source (304) is a success and is not downloaded.
A manual Update of scope ip checks nothing: a feed with a marker is downloaded, another follows the reuse rule; feeds outside the scope are left as they are.
A manual Reload of scope ip parses every feed of the scope again; nothing is checked.
A manual Force download of scope ip hands every feed of the scope to the stage with the force; outside the scope nothing is touched.
cases.departure: Today's Force Check clears the validators (and for both the digests), probes every feed and downloads only a changed one; Core hands the force to the stage (feedstage Change.Force), which downloads every feed of the scope and lets its reuse rule decide the parse.

cases.description: An apply Update probes nothing and reports no outcome; as today's pending apply (a manual pass of scope both) it downloads the feeds whose marker asks for it and reuses the others.
A 304 to the conditional GET is a success, unchanged.
A 200 with the bytes of the baseline is a success, unchanged.
A failed probe leaves the fail marker and no outcome: the occurrence stays pending.
Past the skipfeed limit the feed is not probed: retry-cap-reached, and its fail marker goes.
Hold with a published list is not checked: a success, and a stale fail marker goes.
Hold without a published list is checked like any feed: the missing list is downloaded, with no outcome.
A feed never downloaded is a changed success.
whois and asn feeds are resolved again every run: success, changed, without a probe.
A DNSBL feed is checked the same way, in its own folder.
An IPv6 feed is checked under its _v6 name.
An earlier change left its marker (outside the window): an unchanged answer now does not clear it, and the feed is still downloaded.
A feed with a fail marker is checked though Core did not name it: re-attempted, no outcome.
A retry that names no feed still walks when a fail marker asks for it.
Feeds are checked IPv4, IPv6, DNSBL, groups and feeds in config order, whatever order Core named them in.
A scheduled Update never checks or rebuilds a feed Core did not name, even one with a marker of an earlier change.
Outside the apply window a found change is pending: its marker stays for the apply.
Outside the window with nothing found and nothing pending, the pass still runs (today's no-update pass).
Outside the window an earlier pending change stays pending.
Inside the window an earlier pending change is applied by the pass.
An Extra changed and no feed is due: inside the window the pass runs over every feed, unchecked, as today's pass for a changed Extra does.
An Extra changed and no feed is due: pending outside the window.
No feed named, no marker, no Extra changed: nothing runs.
With nothing changed, an enabled continent still asks for the pass (today's continent rule).
A manual Update of scope dnsbl leaves the IP feeds and their markers alone.
A group updated Never, a Disabled group and a disabled row are not checked.
Core named a feed the settings no longer hold: skipped, no outcome.
The IP feed folder is a symbolic link: Core runs no feed of it and reports no outcome.
cases.departure: Today's pass follows the link. Core refuses a feed folder that is a symbolic link (feedstage.Recover), so no probe or run reads or writes through it.

cases.description: The baseline was replaced by a directory: the feed fails with no outcome and no probe.
cases.departure: Today's check takes any file system entry for the baseline and compares its digest sidecar, so the feed is reported unchanged; Core reads a baseline that is no regular file as unusable and does not settle the occurrence.
